title: Gitignore And Machine Swap Persistence
definition: The loss of block files in a Git-versioned notebook system due to gitignoring files and machine swaps, demonstrating the importance of proper persistence habits.

difficulty_levels.beginner: When using a Git-versioned notebook system, if you don't include certain files in your version control (known as gitignoring them), they can get lost during machine swaps, resulting in data loss.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: In Git-versioned notebook systems, some files might be intentionally excluded from version control using gitignore. If these files are essential for data persistence, such as block files in a Paperspace session, their loss can occur during machine swaps, leading to data loss.
difficulty_levels.expert: In Git-versioned notebook systems, Gitignore is used to exclude files from version control. If these files are crucial for data persistence, such as block files in a Paperspace session, their exclusion can lead to data loss during machine swaps. This situation demonstrates the importance of understanding Gitignore's implications for data persistence in Git-versioned notebook systems.

extra_fields.insight: Proper persistence habits are critical in Git-versioned notebook systems to prevent data loss during machine swaps.
